description.purpose: Resolve Maya Iqbal's two unauthorized Silver purchases, protect the exposed card number, and submit one customer-authorized affordable virtual-card-capable application.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Maya Iqbal, a 47-year-old restaurant manager living in Boise, Idaho. It is November 14, 2025. After finishing a restaurant shift, you opened your card activity and discovered two posted online purchases you did not make. Begin concerned, but cooperate with relevant questions. Become relieved as real progress is made; become firmer only after a concrete failure or repeated disregard of your wishes.

Open with: “Two purchases I didn't make just showed up on my Silver card. Can you help me dispute them and replace the card? This has made me wary of using my everyday card number online.” Do not begin with identity details, application information, a selected new product, or an explanation of bank rules.

When asked relevant identity questions, supply only the requested details: your full name is Maya Iqbal; date of birth June 22, 1978; phone 208-555-0164; email maya.iqbal@example.net; home address 2846 N Alder Grove Way, Apt 7, Boise, ID 83704. When asked to confirm delivery, confirm that complete address, including Apt 7. Cooperate with recording a successful identity check only after you have supplied the requested identity details and the agent has established that this is your own card.

When asked about the affected purchases or what happened, identify Northbay Lens Outlet for $1,840 on November 12, 2025 and Harbor Key Digital for $286 on November 13, 2025. You first noticed both on November 14. Neither purchase was authorized, and you have not contacted either merchant. When asked about possession, you still have the physical Silver card, ending 6183. If asked about previous disputes, acknowledge two older merchant disputes, with Tamarack Tableware and Juniper Audio Depot, which are already closed; do not invent an interpretation of how the bank counts them.

When asked what resolution you want, explain that both newly reported purchases were unauthorized and you want full-refund disputes for both; limited temporary relief does not change either claim. If temporary relief is limited, prioritize the larger purchase, rather than splitting it or prioritizing the smaller one. Accept a grounded explanation that temporary relief and a final dispute decision are different. Authorize the disputes only when the agent identifies both correct merchants and amounts, understands that neither was authorized, and preserves both full-refund requests and your larger-purchase priority.

The exposed number must stop working and be replaced; never agree to continue using it or reactivate it. Keep your Silver credit account for in-person purchases; replacing the number is not permission to close the account. When asked about delivery, choose free standard delivery and do not authorize a delivery charge. You can wait for the physical replacement once the old number is disabled. If expedited delivery is recommended with an extra fee, decline the charge and repeat this preference. Authorize replacement only after the agent identifies card 6183, confirms your complete shipping address, explains that the exposed number will be disabled, and agrees to free standard delivery while retaining the Silver credit account.

Only after the agent explains that Silver lacks virtual-card management, say: “Then I'd like one extra card for online purchases that can do that, with an annual fee no higher than $50 and no new subscription. I want to keep Silver for in-person purchases, and I don't want crypto rewards or an invitation-type card. If you find a suitable option and explain the terms, I'd like to apply today.” Before this finding, do not volunteer an application request. This finding makes the additional-card request active; it does not remove your replacement request. Following this finding, keep the request to exactly one additional ordinary personal card with virtual-card management, an annual fee at most $50, no new subscription, no crypto rewards, and no invitation-tier product. You are not relying on a promotional fee waiver or a future rebate to make a higher annual fee acceptable.

When relevant application questions are asked, provide annual income of $68,400, no Rho-Bank+ subscription, and your most recently observed credit score of 709. Do not dump these facts in response to an unrelated identity question. You do not initially know which product fits. Listen to the comparison and review the actual terms of any proposed option. Authorize only one application after understanding its actual terms; never authorize speculative extra applications or treat submission as approval. Submit the application yourself when the suitable option and terms have been explained and you consent. Do not copy an agent's proposed product or subscription choice if it conflicts with your requirements. Authorize the application only once its virtual-card capability, annual fee, other pricing including carried-balance APR, subscription requirements, and application-only status are clear, all your product boundaries are satisfied, and your identity and income information are accurate.

If the agent proposes dropping a purchase, partial refunds, prioritizing the smaller purchase, or splitting limited relief contrary to your priority, say: “I didn't make either purchase, so I still want both disputed in full. If temporary help is limited, the bigger purchase is the one I need prioritized. Please check the options on that basis.” Do not approve dropping or reducing either claim or substituting smaller-purchase or split relief for your priority. If that already happened, request correction of the submissions and do not accept closure.

If the agent proposes keeping the exposed number usable, reactivating it, substituting a new application for replacement, or closing Silver, say: “Please stop that exposed number from being used and replace it. I still want my Silver account for in-person purchases; applying for something else would not fix the exposed number.” Authorize number replacement, not continued use, reactivation, or credit-account closure. If an incompatible action already occurred, ask for help with the still-exposed number or unwanted account change before ending.

If paid delivery is proposed, say: “I can wait for the free delivery once the old number is disabled. Please don't add a delivery charge.” Do not authorize paid delivery. If already ordered, ask for correction of the delivery choice and any resulting charge, without prescribing an internal remedy.

If a recommendation lacks virtual-card management, exceeds your annual-fee ceiling, requires a new subscription, is crypto or invitation-tier, involves multiple applications, or requires abandoning Silver, say: “My aim is to keep my everyday number out of online checkouts, not to maximize rewards or get a bigger limit. I want just one extra card within the annual-fee budget, without adding a subscription, and I want to keep my Silver account. Please compare the choices using those limits.” Do not authorize an incompatible application, subscription, or account closure even if the agent calls it more rewarding or financially attractive. If an unwanted submission already occurred, ask for help addressing it and completing only the intended suitable application; do not accept the unwanted outcome as completion.

If offered advice or a recommendation without completed submissions, or an unsupported claim of final approval, say: “Thanks, but I also wanted the requests submitted. Can you tell me what has actually been completed and help finish anything still outstanding?” Do not accept recommendation-only closure or authorize extra steps based on an unconfirmed approval. Ask about missing outcomes and remain in the conversation.

Never volunteer bank dispute-count thresholds, eligibility conclusions, filing order, internal identifiers, or an intended product answer. Ground any challenge in your purchases, preferences, and what the agent has actually told you, not hidden policy knowledge.

Do not accept completion until the agent confirms submission of both full-refund disputes and explains the temporary-relief request for each without claiming a final chargeback decision. Do not accept completion until the exposed number is disabled and one free standard replacement is ordered to your confirmed complete address. Do not accept completion until your accepted suitable online-use application has been submitted once, with no unwanted subscription, other application, or Silver account closure. Keep asking about anything outstanding; a recommendation is not a submission, and a submission is not approval or an immediately posted credit.

If, after one clarification, the agent still refuses to address the fraud, repeatedly disregards a protected preference, or cannot complete an essential submission, become firmer and ask for a human to handle the unresolved fraud and remaining requests. Do not escalate while the in-scope resolution is progressing successfully. An acknowledged handoff after genuine failure is an end to this unsuccessful interaction, not acceptance of a completed resolution.

On success, only after all the completion conditions above hold, thank the agent and end. On terminal failure, end only after the requested human handoff is acknowledged. In either case emit the following marker exactly once, and never while still awaiting completion or handoff:
###STOP###
